bangtutorial/bang-motion.readme:
# Bang Motion **An agent skill that turns your AI coding agent into a motion designer.**
Openers, promos, product demos, kinetic typography, and explainers — built as a single `index.html` that plays like video, not like slides. [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.19.0-2f6fd6?style=flat-square)](CHANGELOG.md) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-3fa34d?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Agent Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/format-Agent%20Skills-1c2a4a?style=flat-square)](#install) [![Works with](https://img.shields.io/badge/works%20with-Claude%20Code%20%C2%B7%20Codex%20%C2%B7%20Gemini%20CLI%20%C2%B7%20Cursor-7a5af5?style=flat-square)](#install) [What you can make](#what-you-can-make) · [Style gallery](#style-gallery) · [Workflow](#recommended-workflow) · [Example prompts](#example-prompts) · [Install](#install) · [FAQ](#faq)
--- ## Why Ask an AI agent for "a video" and you usually get **slides**: one section per idea, a title, a photo, a fade between them. Bang Motion encodes what a working motion designer insists on — one continuous world, a camera that actually moves, a subject that persists, text that lives inside the scene — as **rules an agent can check in its own code**, plus starters that make the right architecture the easy path. It also stops every project from looking the same. The look is **derived from your brand** through a required style brief, the structure is **chosen from a menu of concepts**, and nothing is inherited from the starter or copied from a reference. ## What you can make | | Output | Typical length | |---|---|---| | 🎬 **Openers & promos** | product launches, app promos, campaign spots, teasers | 15–40 s | | 🖥️ **Product & SaaS demos** | UI assembled and used on screen, camera following the clicks | 20–60 s | | 🔤 **Kinetic typography** | lyric-style statements, event announcements, manifestos | 10–30 s | | 📺 **Bumpers, idents, channel intros** | short brand moments that loop | 3–10 s | | 🧭 **Explainers** | six explainer styles, optional voice-over sync, 16:9 or 9:16 | 30–120 s | | 🎥 **Video layers** | your own or generated clips placed like footage — inside devices, frames, and masks, locked to the timeline | — | | 🎞️ **After Effects builds** | cartoon explainers built directly inside AE through the Higgsfield MCP bridge | — | Every deliverable is one `index.html`: double-click to play, autoplay + loop, `?debug=1` for a scrub bar, and an optional frame-by-frame export to MP4. ## Style gallery > Each frame below is a **single static scene** built for this README with **fictional brands and data**. The portrait, product photos, port photo, engraving, and cartoon cutouts were generated with GPT Image 2.5; everything else is HTML, CSS, and SVG. Real projects take their palette, type, and imagery from your brand.

Grainy gradient · opener
Glowing layered shapes, soft grain, a camera that travels through them. Tech, AI, music, premium launches.
Poster color-block · kinetic typography
Huge cropped words, solid color fields that slam in on the beat. Events, music, launches.

Product tour with claims · SaaS demo
Real UI lifted out of the dashboard, the camera zooms into what gets clicked. SaaS, dashboards, B2B.
Flat vector illustration · promo
Solid fills, stylized hands, UI drawn flat, shapes with gentle overshoot. Fintech, consumer apps.

Flat pop with photos · promo
Photo cutouts popping in, stickers, brand color fields that change with a visible trigger. Consumer apps, campaigns.
Continuous action · explainer
One subject that never stops, numbers and maps living inside the world. Speed, routes, processes.

Visual journalism · explainer
Black ground, real photos with source tags, highlighter, dashed annotations. News, current issues.
White catalog · explainer
White grid, product cutouts, mixed script and heavy sans. Products, brands.

Vintage sketch · explainer
Sepia paper, engraving art, classic serifs, rust notes. History, biography.
Cartoon collage · explainer
Cream paper, flat illustration cutouts, color pills, handwriting. Science, education.

Cartoon stage · explainer
One living stage per scene, jointed characters, no captions. Education with characters.

filippocalippo/StykAnimate-App.description: Free, open-source stick figure animation app for Windows, Linux and the browser. Opens Pivot and Stick Nodes projects.
filippocalippo/StykAnimate-App.readme:
A free, open-source stick figure animation app for Windows, Linux and the browser.
Opens Pivot (.piv, .stk) and Stick Nodes projects, and keeps your work on your device.

Website · Open in the browser · Download · Discord · YouTube

## Features - **Pose stick figures** with fixed-length joints, IK for arms and legs, stretchy nodes and 3D figures with depth. - **Build your own figures** from lines, circles, polygons, text and images, with a shared rig and per-part styles. - **Two timelines:** a Simple, Pivot-style frame strip and an Advanced timeline with layers, folders, keys and easing. - **Motion paths, onion skins and camera moves,** including camera follow. - **Particle effects** (explosions, auras, beams, smoke) and brushes for drawing. - **Community library:** insert figures and movieclips shared by other animators. - **Export** MP4, WebM (with transparency), GIF, APNG, PNG/JPEG/SVG frames, and editable `.piv`/`.stk`. - **27 interface languages**, light and dark themes, a touch interface for phones and tablets. Everything (decoding, editing, saving and rendering) runs locally. ## Get StykAnimate - **Windows and Linux:** download Setup, Portable or the AppImage from the [releases page](https://github.com/filippocalippo/styk-animate-releases/releases/latest). Installed apps update themselves. - **Browser:** open [app.stykanimate.com](https://app.stykanimate.com). It works offline once loaded. ## Privacy Your animations stay on your computer. The desktop app sends anonymous statistics about speed and crashes and which features are used, with no account, no identifier and nothing from your animations. Home says so in one line at first start, and Preferences › Privacy turns them off and shows exactly what was last sent. [docs/STATISTICS.md](docs/STATISTICS.md) lists everything that is sent and why. ## Build from source Requirements: Node.js 22+ (CI uses 24.11), the Rust toolchain below, and, for development only, Python 3.11+ (CI uses 3.12): it stages the offline video encoder and builds the Windows codec helpers when packaging, and runs the tests of the Python Pivot codec kept as an oracle. The app, desktop and web, contains and needs no Python. Windows and Linux are tested on every change; macOS has an untested build target. ```sh npm ci npm run engine:build # the Rust engine and Pivot codec, into src/engine/pkg/ npm start # desktop app (Electron) npm run serve # or the editor in your browser at http://127.0.0.1:47831 ``` `npm run engine:build` needs `rustup` with the pinned nightly and its source (`rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-09-15 --component rust-src --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`), the stable Rust that `rust-toolchain.toml` names with the same target (rustup installs it on first use), `wasm-bindgen-cli` 0.2.129 (`cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.129 --locked`) and clang for the WebAssembly target. Python runs only the codec's development test oracle (`backend/`, `codecs/`) and the packaging scripts; set `STYK_PYTHON` to choose an interpreter. Packaging, on the matching operating system: ```sh python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements-build.txt npm run engine:build npm run build:video-encoder npm run pack && npm run verify:package npm run dist:win # or dist:linux, dist:mac ``` The browser build: `npm run web:build`, then `npm run web:preview`. See [Web build](docs/WEB.md), [Linux](docs/LINUX.md) and [Touch interface](docs/TOUCH.md). ## Tests ```sh npm run check # syntax, stylesheet lint, locales, engine inventory npm test # unit tests python -m unittest discover -s backend -p "test_*.py" # the Python codec oracle (development only) ``` Browser tests (`tests/*.browser.mjs`) run against `npm run serve` with Chrome or Playwright Chromium, for example `node tests/timeline.browser.mjs`. `npm run test:browser` starts the server and runs them all, or those whose names contain the words you give it (`npm run test:browser -- timeline hotkeys`), and lists which pass, skip or fail. Some tests read a local corpus of Pivot projects that is not distributed; without it they skip and name the missing file (`STYK_REQUIRE_FIXTURES=1` makes them fail instead). Desktop tests and scripts (`tests/*.desktop.mjs`, `scripts/smoke-*.mjs`) open the app in a window; set `STYK_BACKGROUND_WINDOW=1` to open it off-screen without taking focus (packaged builds too). [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml) shows what runs on every pull request. ## How the code is organized | Location | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | `src/editor*.mjs`, `src/pivot/` | Document model, commands, undo/redo, rigs, native evaluation and validation | | `src/engine/engine-stage.mjs`, `src/engine/engine-playback.mjs` | The scene canvas drawn by the engine, playback tickets | | `src/document-transport.mjs` | Bounded document snapshots | | `engine/` | The Rust engine: document store, Pivot and Stick Nodes codecs, evaluation, rendering, editing (`docs/RUST-ENGINE-PORT.md`) | | `src/engine/` | How the app reaches the engine (stage, playback, export, editing) | | `src/import-*.mjs`, `backend/`, `codecs/`, `native/` | Import into the editor, the Python codec kept as a test oracle, native helpers | | `src/document-export*.mjs`, `src/image-*.mjs`, `src/video-export.mjs` | Saving, recovery and image/video export | | `src/app.mjs`, `src/shell/`, `src/ui/`, `src/styles/` | Interface, workspaces, timelines and styles | | `src/locales/`, `src/localization*.mjs` | Tr

![OpenCreator Agent workspace](./docs/images/opencreator-home-en.png) ## Project Overview OpenCreator is built for individuals and teams who want to keep creative and development work running locally. Instead of reimplementing an Agent loop, it uses Codex CLI as the execution engine and adds a stable local Runtime, a visual workspace, and a Desktop host around it. OpenCreator offers two connected ways to work: - **Content workspace**: use visual tools and creation templates for video translation and downloading, image and video generation, voiceovers, article and social post writing, short-video scripting, and stick figure animation. - **Agent conversation**: start and guide creative or development tasks in natural language, organize conversations by project, keep Runs working in the background, and manage approvals, attachments, files, Skills, MCP, schedules, notifications, memory, and diagnostics from one place. Web is the single frontend implementation. Desktop loads the same Web build and adds only capabilities that require the operating system, such as directory selection, window lifecycle, tray behavior, and native notifications. With the same data and content viewport, both platforms share the same general UI and Runtime behavior. ## Project Highlights - 🤖 **Codex Native**: Reuse the Codex Agent loop, models, reasoning, tool calls, conversations, Skills, and MCP without maintaining a second execution engine. - 🚀 **Ready-to-Use Desktop App**: Launch OpenCreator directly from the desktop app with Codex CLI included; the local Runtime starts on demand and prepares a default project automatically. - ⚙️ **Desktop Setup That Reuses Codex**: On first launch, scan your local Codex configuration and offer to reuse a working ChatGPT sign-in or API key setup. A guided form is available for other model providers. - 🔄 **Managed Runtime Components**: Inspect bundled, active, and latest yt-dlp versions, check for updates periodically, and update manually while keeping the current working version available if an update fails. - 🎨 **Multimodal Creation**: Create and manage video, images, audio, subtitles, and documents through one connected workflow. - 🧩 **Creation Templates**: Start creating images and videos from reusable templates without setting up prompts and settings from scratch. - 🔗 **Dual-Mode Workflow**: Work through either the visual workspace or Agent conversation while one shared state machine keeps steps, progress, and results synchronized. - 🕘 **Versioning**: Every revision creates a new version while preserving earlier settings and outputs for review and comparison. - 🧩 **Reusable Skills**: Use video workflow Skills, extend the Agent with your own Skills, and manage MCP through Codex-native configuration. - 🧠 **Memory**: Keep global, project, and thread memory with summaries and reproducible Run input snapshots. - 🔐 **Local Security**: Keep data, attachments, and logs local by default, with approvals and redacted diagnostics. - 🌐 **Localized Interface**: Use Web and Desktop in 43 interface languages, with automatic system-language detection, manual selection, and right-to-left layouts for Arabic, Persian, Urdu, and Hebrew. ## Creator Tools The current release includes ten creator tools. Available models and services depend on your local Codex environment and AI service settings. mromidev/claude-animated-shorts.description: Free Claude skill: viral animated story shorts (2D characters in a 3D world) with three.js + Remotion
mromidev/claude-animated-shorts.readme:
# Claude Animated Shorts

The free Claude skill from the video **"How to Make Viral Animated Shorts Using Claude (Full Workflow)"**.

It makes 55-70 s vertical animated story shorts: 2D characters in a colourful 3D world, with ink outlines, a painted town, lens blur, gliding cameras, a march score and sound effects. Everything is rendered with three.js inside Remotion on your own PC, with no AI video generator.

Proven on **The Bridge That Fell for a Song**, a 67 s short about the 1831 Broughton bridge.

## What's inside
| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | The skill: the full pipeline, every rule, every fix, and the final look values |
| `templates/bridge/` | The full source of the bridge short: world, characters, ink, lens blur, grade, story/camera |
| `templates/audio/` | The synthesized sound: SFX, march music, the mix with ducking and loudness |
| `templates/scripts/` | Stills, side-by-side sheets, shot merge and frame-by-frame QA helpers |
| `references/STYLE_BIBLE.md` | The script and visual formula measured from 20 reference shorts |
| `references/reports/` | Seven measured reports: motion, depth, textures, characters, lighting, outlines, grade |
| `references/frames/` | 38 full-size reference frames (540x960) to compare your frames against |
| `references/sheets/` | 20 contact sheets, one per reference short, 60 frames each (1,200 frames) |

## Install
1. Copy this folder to `~/.claude/skills/cartoon-3d-short/` (clone it there, or download the ZIP).
2. You need [Remotion](https://www.remotion.dev/) with `@remotion/three`, plus Node, Python 3 and ffmpeg.
3. In Claude Code, say: *"Use the cartoon short skill and make a short about …"*.

Claude then follows `SKILL.md`: topic and facts, then script, then voice, then the shot plan in `story.ts`, then stills, then renders. Agents check your frames against the reports and the frames, and you get the final 2K render and sound mix.

## Notes
- Set `REMOTION_TMP` to a folder on a big drive. Every Remotion bundle copies `public/` (~1.3 GB) into the temp folder.
- Story, characters and voice should always be your own. Use the references for the look, not the content.

## License
The code and docs are MIT (see `LICENSE`). The reference frames are included for style study only.

howznguyen/shorts-kit.readme: # shorts-kit [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.knowns.dev) [![Facebook group](https://img.shields.io/badge/Facebook-Agentic%20Coding%20Vietnam-1877F2?logo=facebook&logoColor=white)](https://www.facebook.com/groups/agentic.coding.vietnam) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE) ![shorts-kit: narrated shorts and product promos, vertical or landscape, made with your coding agent](docs/assets/cover.webp) Make narrated vertical shorts (TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Reels), and product promos in 9:16 or 16:9, with a coding agent and [Remotion](https://www.remotion.dev). You talk to your agent ("make a video about why the sky is blue"). The agent follows the kit's skills step by step: facts first, a storytelling flow, the script, the voice, the scenes, stills to check, the render, the cover and the caption. You review, then you upload the file yourself. The kit never posts anything. The rules and skills come from a private pipeline that took a new knowledge channel from zero to about 120k views on its best video in two months. Every rule keeps the reason it exists, because most of them were written after a published video broke it. They are defaults: change them for your own channel. ## Results The channel these rules came from, two months in. The best videos and the flops sit side by side on purpose: topics close to the audience carried it (tens of thousands of views), topics that drifted from the channel's niche got a few hundred. The kit cannot pick your topic for you. ![A TikTok profile grid: 122.1K, 63.3K, 48.4K, 31.7K and 11.8K views next to 3,692, 768, 349 and 232](docs/assets/tiktok-results.jpg) What a finished run reports, from the original private pipeline (it also copied files to a NAS and applied that channel's own swearing rule; neither is part of this kit): ![An agent's end-of-run report: narration, TTS, scenes, render, loudness and encode, cover, caption, hand-off, and the fact checks it caught](docs/assets/agent-run.jpg) ## What is in the box - **10 agent skills** (`.claude/skills/sk-*`), started by `sk-pipeline` (shorts) or `sk-promo` (ads and launch films). They work in Claude Code, and in any agent that reads `AGENTS.md` (Codex, OpenCode, ...). - **SOUL.md**: your channel's rulebook. Voice, sentence style, writing for a text-to-speech voice, safe zones, captions, audio, facts, covers, hand-off. Each rule is tagged `[measured]`, `[default]`, `[craft]` or `[hard]` so you know how freely to change it. - **20 storytelling flows** (`docs/flows/`): Three reasons, Trace back, Explain it, Reading a graph, Empty world with a late reveal, and more. Each has beats, when to use it and its traps. - **A fact ledger** (`docs/facts/`). No sentence goes into a script before its claim has a verified record, and the linter enforces it. - **A Remotion library** (`src/shared/`): word-timed captions, kinetic type, safe-zone overlay, music bed and SFX, camera moves, and an illustrated world (sky, sea, sun, moon, stars, clouds, rain, birds, people, fish). - **Maps and a globe** (`src/shared/map/`): satellite imagery with a camera that flies from country to street and stays sharp, coastlines, borders and rivers from Natural Earth, routes that draw on, pins, measured distances, filled regions, a ready Vietnam map with the Hoàng Sa and Trường Sa archipelagos, a 3D globe with great-circle lines, and a pull-out from any scene to the globe. - **Shared graphics** for any video: strike-and-replace, slot word, word slam, typewriter, hand-drawn circles, arrows, underlines, cross-outs and stamps, and charts that stay true to scale (compare bars, progress ring, unit grid, odometer). Browse them with `bun run dev gallery`. - **Your own voice or footage instead of TTS** (`bun run ingest`, `bun run cut`): Whisper transcribes the recording, fillers, retakes and long silences are proposed as cuts, and the cut voice drives the video like a TTS voice would. Film yourself (`talking-head`, the take is the background and effects stay off your face) or bring a voice recording only. The words stay what was said: every claim in them still needs a verified fact. See [docs/visuals/talking-head.md](docs/visuals/talking-head.md). - **Product promos** (`sk-promo`, `docs/promo/`): the gates an agency would run, in order: objective and placement, the user's pain first, concept routes, a confirmed treatment, a timed animatic with the real music on a measured beat grid (`bun run beats`) and a scratch voice (`bun run voice`), a shot-by-shot storyboard, then the build, cutdowns (15 s, 6 s) and a stranger comprehension test. Vertical feed ads and 16:9 launch films. - **A shot library** (`docs/shots/`): 160+ named motion recipes (camera, typography, UI entrances, rhythm, transitions, effects, outros, isometric piles, real typed search), each with parameters in frames, and sound cards for the SFX pack. Storyboard shots name their card. ![Twelve shot cards' demos playing at once: kinetic type, card flips, a 3D camera, transitions, a neon frame, a 3D carousel, a card stack, gauges, type assembly, a slam entrance, element moves and a beat cut](docs/assets/shots.webp) - **Real interface components** in films (`docs/promo/real-ui.md`): Knowns UI by default, or a product's own components copied from its repo, driven frame by frame, deterministic (a render twice gives the same file); `bun run capture` for real pages (`--type` to type into the page's own search, `--hide` for overlays). - **3D**: a Three.js scene kit (`src/shared/three/`: shots, camera rigs, callouts glued to a model) and procedural models built headless with Blender (`bun run model`), plus CSS-3D isometric piles and turns (`src/shared/motion/iso.tsx`). - **8 CC0 sound effects** generated by the kit (`public/sfx/`)

sonlovinbot-team/Muse-animated-short-fil.description: Skill làm phim hoạt hình ngắn trên Muse AI — từ ý tưởng đến MP4: nhân vật, kịch bản, keyframes, mega prompt, video, thuyết minh, dựng phim. Phim mẫu: The Last Lantern.
sonlovinbot-team/Muse-animated-short-fil.readme:
# 🎬 Muse Animated Short Film

[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/sonlovinbot/Muse-animated-short-film?style=social)](https://github.com/sonlovinbot/Muse-animated-short-film/stargazers)
 🌐 **Trang giới thiệu: https://app.danghuuson.com/Muse-animated-short-film/**

![The Last Lantern — phim mẫu làm bằng skill này](docs/assets/poster.jpg)

**Tác giả:** Đặng Hữu Sơn ([sonlovinbot](https://github.com/sonlovinbot)) — CEO & Co-Founder LovinBot AI

Skill dựng phim hoạt hình ngắn **từ đầu đến cuối trên Muse AI** — từ một ý tưởng thô thành file MP4 hoàn chỉnh: nhân vật, kịch bản, hình ảnh, video, thuyết minh và dựng phim.

*An end-to-end skill for producing animated short films on Muse AI — from a raw idea to a finished MP4.*

> [!TIP]
> Thấy skill có ích? Bấm **⭐ Star** ở góc trên repo — giúp nhiều người làm phim tìm thấy skill này hơn.

## 🎥 Video giới thiệu

[![Video giới thiệu Muse AI](docs/assets/video-thumbnail.jpg)](https://youtu.be/kysOeBo5Qtw)

Muse AI — tạo ảnh, video, audio — có cảnh từ phim mẫu "The Last Lantern". Xem trên YouTube: https://youtu.be/kysOeBo5Qtw

## Skill này làm gì?

![Quy trình 8 bước](docs/assets/pipeline.svg)

Pipeline đã kiểm chứng qua dự án thật "The Last Lantern" (8 cảnh, 2D Disney/Pixar):

| # | Giai đoạn | Kết quả |
|---|-----------|---------|
| 0 | Thu thập đầu vào | Thời lượng → số cảnh, ngôn ngữ, tỷ lệ 16:9/9:16 |
| 1 | Character sheets | Khóa nhân vật (nhiều góc + biểu cảm) |
| 2 | Story bible | Chốt kịch bản: logline, character lock, từng cảnh |
| 3 | Keyframes | K1..K(N+1), luật match-cut |
| 4 | Mega prompt | 1 prompt copy-paste cho mỗi cảnh |
| 5 | Generate video | Từng clip first-frame → last-frame |
| 6 | Làm VO | Kịch bản thuyết minh kiểu kể chuyện |
| 7 | Dựng phim | ffmpeg: normalize, nối, mix VO |

Kèm theo: **luật realism** (hành động vật lý phải đúng thực tế), **STRICT ASPECT RATIO LOCK** (ref đầu vào phải cùng tỷ lệ với output), và **10+ bài học xương máu**.

## 🏮 Tác phẩm mẫu: "The Last Lantern"

Bộ file thật của dự án — mở ra là thấy mỗi giai đoạn trông như thế nào: [`examples/the-last-lantern/`](examples/the-last-lantern/)

| Milo | Lyra | Ember |
|---|---|---|
| ![Milo](docs/assets/characters/milo-sheet.jpg) | ![Lyra](docs/assets/characters/lyra-sheet.jpg) | ![Ember](docs/assets/characters/ember-sheet.jpg) |

| K1 · mở đầu | K2 | K3 | K7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![K1](docs/assets/keyframes/k1-city-dusk.jpg) | ![K2](docs/assets/keyframes/k2-spark-falls.jpg) | ![K3](docs/assets/keyframes/k3-ember-sneeze.jpg) | ![K7](docs/assets/keyframes/k7-door-light.jpg) |

| File | Nội dung |
|---|---|
| [`STORY.md`](examples/the-last-lantern/STORY.md) | Story bible: logline, thế giới, character lock, 8 nhịp cảnh, mô-típ nhạc |
| [`MEGA_PROMPTS.md`](examples/the-last-lantern/MEGA_PROMPTS.md) | 8 mega prompt copy-paste + thứ tự nạp ref + ghi chú dựng |
| [`VO_SCRIPT.md`](examples/the-last-lantern/VO_SCRIPT.md) | Thuyết minh Anh – Việt, mốc thời gian |
| [`FLOW.md`](examples/the-last-lantern/FLOW.md) | Dự án đi qua 8 giai đoạn: việc làm, file ra, điểm chốt, chuỗi keyframe |

## Cách dùng (cho người mới)

1. **Cài skill:** copy cả folder này vào thư mục skills của Muse AI, VD: `~/workspace/skills/animated-short-film/`
   - Hoặc: dán link repo này vào chat Muse, Muse sẽ tự cài.
2. **Mở chat và nói:** "Tôi muốn làm phim hoạt hình ngắn."
3. **Trả lời 3 câu hỏi đầu tiên:** phim dài bao lâu? ngôn ngữ nào? tỷ lệ 16:9 hay 9:16?
4. **Duyệt ở các điểm chốt:** mô tả nhân vật → story bible → keyframes → từng video → VO → phim cuối. Bạn chỉ việc xem và nói "ok" hoặc "sửa chỗ này".

Bạn không cần đọc các file reference — Muse tự đọc khi cần. Mọi prompt kỹ thuật, câu lệnh generate và dựng phim đã nằm trong skill.

## Cấu trúc

```
├── SKILL.md                  # Quy trình + luật vận hành (Muse đọc)
├── README.md                 # File này (người đọc)
├── references/               # Hướng dẫn chi tiết từng giai đoạn
│   ├── 01-character-sheets.md
│   ├── 02-story-and-script.md
│   ├── 03-keyframes.md
│   ├── 04-mega-prompts.md
│   ├── 05-video-generation.md
│   ├── 06-vo-production.md
│   ├── 07-assembly.md
│   └── 08-lessons.md
├── examples/
│   └── the-last-lantern/     # Tác phẩm mẫu: STORY, MEGA_PROMPTS, VO_SCRIPT, FLOW
└── docs/                     # Trang giới thiệu (GitHub Pages) + ảnh minh hoạ
    └── assets/
```

## ⭐ Ủng hộ

Nếu skill giúp bạn làm được bộ phim đầu tiên, hãy **[star repo](https://github.com/sonlovinbot/Muse-animated-short-film)** và chia sẻ phim của bạn. Các phần mềm, game 3D và tài liệu AI miễn phí khác: **[app.danghuuson.com](https://app.danghuuson.com)**

## Giấy phép

MIT — dùng tự do, ghi credit tác giả khi chia sẻ lại. Xem [LICENSE](LICENSE).

useapi/muse-api.readme:
# Meta Muse API examples (useapi.net): AI video, images and agent chat on muse.ai

English · [中文](#中文说明) · [日本語](#日本語の説明) · [Português](#sobre-este-repositório) · [Tiếng Việt](#về-repo-này) · [Bahasa Indonesia](#tentang-repo-ini) · [ไทย](#เกี่ยวกับ-repo-นี้)

Runnable examples for the [Muse API](https://useapi.net/docs/api-muse-v1?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api) by [useapi.net](https://useapi.net/?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api): make images and 10-second videos with sound using Muse (muse.ai), Meta's AI agent, through a REST API that runs on your [Muse subscription](https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/): Free, Power $20 or Maximum $100 a month (as of October 2026). Combine up to 9 photos into one picture, restore and colorize old photos, animate a still with spoken dialogue, and replace a person in a video. Every file Muse makes is an asset id the next job takes as an input, so edits chain with no downloads or re-uploads.

Demo on YouTube: [Meta Muse API Demo: Images, Talking Photos, Video with Sound, Chat & MCP (third-party, useapi.net)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OMUGbfRIO5E)

| Example | What it does | Tutorial | Tutorial date |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`images-videos/`](./images-videos) | Three photos become one picture of a rider on a vintage motorcycle in the surf, the picture becomes a 10-second video in which she shouts a line, and a woman from a fourth photo replaces her in that video. Also two images from text, and a hundred-year-old portrait restored, colorized and brought to life. Node.js and Python | [How to Generate AI Videos and Images with the Meta Muse API](https://useapi.net/docs/articles/muse-images-videos?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api) | October 12, 2026 |
| [`narrated-short/`](./narrated-short) | Narrated 30-second Short from a topic: a chat writes the script as JSON, three 9:16 video jobs run at once with the same off-screen narrator speaking each line, and a last chat joins the clips with ffmpeg into one MP4. About 2 to 3 minutes per Short. Optional fixed voice through Muse text to speech. Node.js and Python | [Make a 30-second narrated Short](https://useapi.net/docs/articles/muse-images-videos?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api#make-a-30-second-narrated-short-script-three-scenes-one-join) | October 18, 2026 |
| [`demo/`](./demo) | **Live chat app**: one self-contained HTML page that chats with the Muse agent through the API, with answers streamed live, files and cards, approvals, several live chats at once, workspace files and the agent's permissions. Open the [live demo](https://useapi.net/demos/muse/?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api) or open `demo/index.html` locally. Vanilla JS, no build | [Chat Streaming Guide](https://useapi.net/docs/api-muse-v1/chat-streaming-guide?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api) | October 12, 2026 |
| [`skills/muse-video/`](./skills/muse-video) | **Agent skill** for Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents: ask for an image or a clip and the agent makes it with Muse (text to image, photo compositing, old-photo restoration, talking photos, person swap in a video) and downloads the `.webp` or `.mp4`, never paying twice for a request. Install: `npx skills add useapi/muse-api --skill muse-video`. Bash, curl, jq | [SKILL.md](./skills/muse-video/SKILL.md) | October 12, 2026 |
| [`n8n/`](./n8n) | **n8n app**: upload an old photo, Muse restores and colorizes it, you pick or redo, then the person in it says your line in a 10-second video with sound. 1 or 2 takes, the real share of the week used on the result page, optional Google Drive save, and a Google Sheet batch mode. Core n8n nodes, no community nodes. Plus **narrated faceless Shorts** from a topic: a script page, one narrated 9:16 scene per part, joined and saved to Google Drive | [n8n template #20989](https://n8n.io/workflows/20989), [#21207](https://n8n.io/workflows/21207) | October 19, 2026 |
| [MCP server](#mcp-server) | **Hosted MCP server**: connect Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Windsurf to `https://api.useapi.net/v1/muse/mcp` and the assistant gets 37 tools for Muse images, videos, chat, files and permissions. Nothing to install or host | [MCP Server](https://useapi.net/docs/api-muse-v1/mcp?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api) | October 13, 2026 |

## Quick start

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) v21 or newer **or** [Python](https://www.python.org) 3.x (no dependencies to install), a useapi.net [API token](https://useapi.net/docs/start-here/setup-useapi?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api), and a Muse account (free or paid) added with the [Muse setup](https://useapi.net/docs/start-here/setup-muse?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/useapi/muse-api.git
cd muse-api/images-videos
node ./images-videos.mjs <API_TOKEN> <EMAIL>
# or, equivalently, with Python:
python3 ./images-videos.py <API_TOKEN> <EMAIL>
# just one image and one video (restore an old photo, then make it talk):
node ./images-videos.mjs <API_TOKEN> <EMAIL> --steps portrait-video
```

Each example's README lists its options. Every endpoint is documented in the [Muse API reference](https://useapi.net/docs/api-muse-v1?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-api).

It has 37 tools: generate images and videos, chat with the Muse agent, answer its permission requests, open a live view of its web browser, manage the account's Library and files, and reset the account. Each tool calls the Muse API, so the same rules, limits and allowance apply. Nothin

Muse AI

OpenAI-compatible API gateway for muse.ai personal workspaces, featuring native 9Router integration.

--- ## Architecture ```text OpenAI SDK / 9Router / Web Client │ ▼ HTTP (Bearer Token) ┌──────────────┐ │ Muse AI │ FastAPI Proxy (Port 18610) └──────┬───────┘ │ Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP over WebSocket) ▼ ┌──────────────┐ │ Chromium │ Headless Browser (Isolated Context per Account) └──────┬───────┘ │ HTTPS / WSS (hatch_sess + hatch_gw + datr) ▼ muse.ai ``` --- ## Technical Highlights - **OpenAI Wire Compatibility**: Direct drop-in for OpenAI SDKs, LangChain, LobeChat, NextChat, Cherry Studio, and autonomous coding agents. - **Native 9Router Provider**: Ships with `scripts/connect_9router.py` to auto-register model routes directly into 9Router's SQLite database (`~/.9router/db/data.sqlite`). - **Resilient Cookie Injection**: Automatically URL-decodes percent-encoded cookie tokens (`%3A` -> `:`) and registers sessions across dual-domain scopes (`.muse.ai` and `muse.ai`) via CDP. - **Meta Edge Proxy Compliance**: Supports `datr` cookie passing to prevent device-integrity redirects on Meta infrastructure. - **Account Pooling & Failover**: Multi-account scheduling (`affinity`, `lru`, `round_robin`), concurrency limits, automatic error cooldown, and transparent retries. - **Deterministic Offline Testing**: 100% offline test suite powered by `MockDriver` (23 passed in < 0.5s). --- ## Quickstart ### 1. Installation Requires Python 3.10+ and a local Chromium or Google Chrome binary. ```bash git clone https://github.com/d4ncboz/museai.git cd museai python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install -e '.[dev]' ``` ### 2. Configuration Copy the example environment configuration: ```bash cp .env.example .env ``` Default settings in `.env`: ```ini MUSEAI_DRIVER=browser MUSEAI_HOST=127.0.0.1 MUSEAI_PORT=18610 MUSEAI_API_KEY=sk-museai-local-key MUSEAI_ADMIN_KEY=sk-museai-admin-key MUSEAI_POOL_STRATEGY=affinity MUSEAI_KEEPALIVE_ENABLED=true ``` *(Note: Chrome executable is auto-detected on macOS `/Applications/Google Chrome.app` and Linux `/usr/bin/chromium`. Set `MUSEAI_CHROMIUM_PATH` if using a custom path).* ### 3. Run the Service ```bash python -m museai ``` The server binds to `http://127.0.0.1:18610`. --- ## Authentication & Account Setup ### 1. Account Registration An active [muse.ai](https://muse.ai) account is required. If you do not have an account yet, follow the step-by-step registration guide here: - **Registration Guide**: [Telegram @bozdrop/8447](https://t.me/bozdrop/8447) ### 2. Export Session Cookies Export your session cookies from an active [muse.ai](https://muse.ai) browser session (DevTools `F12` ──> `Application` ──> `Cookies` ──> `https://muse.ai`): - `hatch_sess`: Session authentication token - `hatch_gw`: Gateway routing cookie - `hatch_native_auth_device`: Registered device UUID - `hatch_vml`: Workspace lease token *(optional/dynamic)* - `datr`: Meta device verification cookie *(recommended)* ### Import via Admin API ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18610/admin/accounts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-museai-admin-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "label": "primary-account", "cookies": { "hatch_sess": "...", "hatch_gw": "...", "hatch_native_auth_device": "...", "hatch_vml": "...", "datr": "..." } }' ``` Alternatively, use the helper script to convert raw Netscape / DevTools JSON exports: ```bash python scripts/extract_cookies.py exported_cookies.txt --label primary-account --out account.json curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18610/admin/accounts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-museai-admin-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d @account.json ``` --- ## 9Router Multi-Model Gateway Hook To register `museai` into a local [9Router](https://github.com/9router/9router) instance: ```bash python scripts/connect_9router.py --port 18610 --api-key sk-museai-local-key --prefix muse ``` Call the model through 9Router immediately: ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "muse/muse-chat", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "ping"}] }' ``` Available model IDs routed by 9Router: - `muse/muse-chat`: Primary personal agent conversational model - `muse/gpt-4o`: OpenAI tooling alias - `muse/gpt-5`: High-reasoning alias - `muse/claude-sonnet-4`: Sonnet alias - `muse/muse-video`: Text / first-frame image-to-video --- ## API Usage ### Streaming Chat Completion (`curl`) ```bash curl -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18610/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-museai-local-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "muse-chat", "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise engineering assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Explain raft consensus in two sentences."} ], "stream": true }' ``` ### Python SDK (`openai`) ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( base_url="http://127.0.0.1:18610/v1", api_key="sk-museai-local-key" ) response = client.chat.completions.create( model="muse-chat", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a thread-safe singleton in Py

sarpstar/cinecode.description: Films made with code. Short films, long YouTube videos, ads, explainers and music videos: an AI coding agent writes the script, builds every frame in code, designs the sound and hands you an MP4.
sarpstar/cinecode.readme:
Kodla yazılmış filmler.
Kısa filmler, uzun YouTube videoları, reklamlar, açıklayıcılar ve müzik videoları. Fikri ve zevki sen getirirsin; bir yapay zekâ kodlama ajanı senaryoyu yazar, her kareyi kodla kurar, sesi tasarlar ve sana bitmiş bir MP4 verir.

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · Kurulum · Hızlı başlangıç · SSS

cinecode ile yapılmış filmlerden 30 saniye. Her kare başsız Chrome'da koddan üretildi.

Kendi bilgisayarında çalışır: en iyi **Claude Code**'da (masaüstü uygulaması, VS Code eklentisi, terminal), ayrıca **Cursor**'da; kullanıcılar Codex ve Antigravity gibi başka ajanlarda da çalıştırdı. Ücretli bir servis gerekmez; dış ses, yalnızca istersen, kendi Gemini anahtarını (ücretsiz kotası var), ElevenLabs'i ya da ücretsiz bir Türkçe sesi kullanır. ## Neler yapabilirsin ### Kodla yapılmış kısa filmler Aklındakini tek cümleyle yaz; gerisini birlikte kurarsınız. - **Sıradan fikirde kalmaz.** Ajan fikrini, dünyadan rastgele çekilen gerçek bir şeyle buluşturur: bir müze eseri, bir hayvan, uzaydan bir fotoğraf, eski bir icat, tarihî bir yer, bir zanaat. Böylece sana herkesin aklına ilk gelen filmi değil, fikrinin senin bile düşünmediğin yorumlarını getirir. - **Kendini tekrar etmez.** Her öneri senin daha önce yaptığın filmlerle karşılaştırılır; aynı filmi sana ikinci kez önermez. - **Son söz hep senin.** Filmin neyden yapılacağını sen seçersin: gerçek ışıklı 3B, 2B animasyon, boya, mürekkep, kâğıt, kil, hareketli grafik ya da piksel. Görünümü gerçek filmlerden karelerle kurulmuş bir panodan seçersin; film bütünüyle kurulmadan önce ilk iki sahneyi görüp onaylarsın. ### Uzun YouTube videoları On dakikayı aşan belgeseller, açıklayıcılar ve video denemeleri; Film modunda perdeler ve bölümler hâlinde kurulur: - gerçek bir kişi ya da olay hakkındaki her iddianın kaynağıyla yazıldığı, araştırılmış bir metin; - ilk dakikada kurulan açık bir soru ve izleyiciyi sona kadar tutan bir merak haritası; - senin dilinde bir anlatıcı (Türkçe ve İngilizce sesler, ücretsiz Türkçe sesler dahil), çiğ motor sesiyle değil, filme ait bir ses işlemesiyle; - açık arşivlerden fotoğraflar, haritalar, belgeler ve görüntüler; resmi olmayan yerde kod: kendini çizen haritalar, sayaçlar, şemalar, yeniden kurulan mekânlar; - biçim isterse bölüm kartları, her perde için kulakla seçilen müzik, −14 LUFS mastering ve video açıklaman için bir künye dosyası. ### Reklam ve ürün filmleri Ürünün, renklerin, fontların, logon ve çağrı cümlen. Ürün ayrıntısıyla kurulur ve stüdyo çekimi gibi aydınlatılır; yazılım için arayüz kahraman planları; özgüllük testi filmin başka bir markaya uymasını önler; 9:16, 1:1 ve 16:9 sürümleri güvenli alanlarıyla gelir. ### Sosyal medya için açıklayıcılar 30–60 saniyelik dikey filmler: ilk saniyede bir soru, açık lisanslı ve Türkçesi denenmiş bir font eşleşmesiyle kinetik yazı, çizgi çizgi kurulan şemalar, telefonda okunan sözcükler. ### Müzik videoları Şarkını getir: vuruş ızgarası ölçülür, kesmeler ölçülere, vurgular vuruşlara oturur, her söz satırına bir görüntü. ### Ve dahası - **Sevdiğin bir video gibi ama farklı:** biçimi ölçülür (kesmeler, tempo, ışık, renk), film o biçimle yeniden yapılır, onun karelerinden asla. - **Kendi çekimlerinin kurgusu:** konuşan kafa ya da ekran kaydı, kelime zamanlı bir dökümden kesilir; duraklamalar kırpılır, grafikler sözcüklere oturur. - **Tek formatta seri:** bir filmin formatını kaydedip sonraki bölümü o formatta yaparsın. 15 saniyelik bir klipten on dakikayı aşan filmlere kadar. Hızlı mod yaklaşık 3 dakikaya kadar bir filmi tek oturumda yapar; Film modu daha uzun filmleri onaylı adımlarla götürür. Film uzadıkça daha çok zaman ve kullanım ister. ## cinecode ile yapılanlar <
